title: Personal Checking: Extended Overdraft, Restriction and Charge-Off Day Counts
content:
## Overview

When a Personal Checking ledger balance goes below zero and stays there, three milestones are measured in consecutive calendar days of negative balance. This schedule gives the day counts and the one-time charge attached to the first milestone.

| Tier | Extended overdraft fee (USD, once per negative episode) | Days negative before that fee | Days negative before restriction | Days negative before charge-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Student Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Everyday Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Interest Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Premier Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Private Client Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |

## Meaning of each column

- **Extended overdraft fee** — a single charge per negative episode, applied once the balance has been negative for the stated number of calendar days.
- **Days negative before that fee** — how long, in unbroken calendar days below zero, the balance must stay overdrawn for the extended overdraft fee to come due.
- **Days negative before restriction** — the unbroken run of overdrawn calendar days that leads to the account being restricted.
- **Days negative before charge-off** — the unbroken run of overdrawn calendar days that leads to the remaining deficit being charged off.

## The timeline as a single picture

Every tier uses the same three day counts, 7, 30 and 60; only the size of the extended overdraft fee differs. Everyday, Interest and Premier Checking charge 25.00 USD at the first milestone, while Access, Student and Private Client Checking charge nothing there.

Hypothetical illustration: on a Premier Checking account whose balance first went negative on a given day and never recovered, the fee milestone is reached 7 calendar days later, restriction 30 days later and charge-off 60 days later, each count running from that same starting day.
